signals.thesis: Following its record $107.3 billion IPO and private placement pricing at $83 a share, Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, initially lifting U.S. equity futures as gray markets pointed to a jump above 20%. However, the debut failed to halt a broader AI and technology sell-off: the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.3% on Thursday in a volatile session, and the rout spread to Asian tech stocks on Friday as SoftBank shares plunged more than 16%.
signals.title: Nasdaq drops 2.3% and SoftBank plunges 16% as Anthropic debut fails to halt AI sell-off

signals.thesis: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit and agreed to boost global fuel supplies. While the leaders also discussed Ukraine and denuclearization, the talks yielded few other concrete results.
signals.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin agree to boost global fuel supplies at Shenzhen trilateral summit

signals.thesis: Expanding regulatory and market scrutiny beyond earlier federal probes into Nvidia, AMD shares closed down over 7% after a short seller alleged its firmware appeared at a blacklisted Chinese company, though AMD stated it complies with U.S. law. Meanwhile, California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued a subpoena to Nvidia in an investigation into China chip diversion, and Rep. Brian Mast disclosed that the Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies as lawmakers push for tighter export controls.
signals.title: AMD drops 7% on China short report as California subpoenas Nvidia and Congress scrutinizes 879K chip approvals

signals.thesis: Following an earlier slowdown in outbound liquefied natural gas tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran has intensified its attacks on oil tankers crossing the waterway. The escalation comes even as crude oil prices have slid amid surging Middle East supply.
signals.title: Iran intensifies Strait of Hormuz oil tanker attacks amid sliding crude prices

signals.thesis: Japan's core inflation, which excludes food prices, rose to its highest level this year after the expiration of household energy subsidies pushed up consumer prices, though the reading came in below the 2.3% expected by economists. The price acceleration follows a third-quarter contraction in Japan's economy driven by elevated energy costs.
signals.title: Japan core inflation hits year high after energy subsidies expire
